Codex review: needs maintainer review before merge. ## What this changes This PR separates shutdown admission fencing from authority retirement so accepted ingress messages retain restart custody. **Example:** Two accepted app messages await execution when the Gateway receives SIGTERM. - **Before:** Shutdown cancels their authority before restart markers capture them, so neither queued write resumes. - **After:** The replacement Gateway completes both writes in FIFO order, subject to the original limits and current permissions. ## Review scores | Measure | Result | What it means | |---|---|---| | **Overall readiness** | 🦞 diamond lobster **(5/6)** | Focused owner-level repair with shipped CLI restart and forbidden-effect proof, meaningful persistence regressions, and no actionable findings. | | **Proof confidence** | 🦞 diamond lobster **(5/6)** | Sufficient (terminal): The compiled CLI in an isolated Linux VM exercises normal shutdown and a distinct replacement process with fresh relay authentication: two queued writes complete in FIFO order, while role downgrade, People removal, and app revocation prevent late writes. The final head changes only a fixture and allocation. External services use deterministic fixtures; app revocation does not eagerly close an existing provider stream, but its late tool effect is refused. | | **Patch quality** | 🦞 diamond lobster **(5/6)** | No actionable review findings were identified. | ## Product **Kind:** Bug fix · **Worth it:** Yes · **Fix scope:** Complete **User problem:** An app reports a message accepted, but restarting the Gateway silently cancels it before recovery records it. **Reason:** The maintainer-authored change restores the documented graceful-restart contract using existing owners and preserves current authorization. ## Merge readiness ✅ **Ready for maintainer review** Keep open: this maintainer-authored PR repairs a current shutdown-ordering bug that loses accepted queued messages. No actionable source defects remain; exact-head CI is still pending. **Priority:** P2 **Reviewed head:** `edb5215fe19524918581f59698d96af2f9738a51` ## Before merge None. ## Findings None.
Agent review details ### How this fits together Trusted plugins bind principals to Gateway ingress; accepted inputs enter the session queue, shutdown records their existing recovery metadata, and startup restores them through current authorization. ```mermaid flowchart TD A[App principal] --> B[Request admission] B --> C[Accepted session queue] C --> D[Restart custody marker] D --> E[Current authority checks] E --> F[Agent execution and effects] ``` ### Technical review Best possible solution: Keep admission fenced while existing session owners record restart custody, then retire retained authority without weakening live permission checks. Do we have a high-confidence way to reproduce the issue? The supplied compiled CLI receipts establish the base failure, and current-main source exposes the premature authority-abort path; this read-only review executed no target code. Is this the best way to solve the issue? The patch repairs shutdown ordering at the existing lifecycle, request-entry, scheduler, and ingress owners, with no competing recovery implementation or unnecessary production layer. AGENTS.md: found and applied where relevant. Codex review notes: model internal, reasoning medium; reviewed against [aa4ebbb626c4](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/aa4ebbb626c4dd6f5fad85e7bfc34d10e8c103fc). ### Provenance checked - `Principal-bound ingress authority` keeps the original intent (2444aae8f8f9e593f4801127eab4b37d3703c4c6: Trusted plugins require principal-bound access under current roles and session visibility; later merged membership repairs retain the approving source.) - `Request-entry lifetime` keeps the original intent (3ed226a746a8efd223a35a81790014c41ff044a3: Fence new preparation and join admitted work before tearing down dependencies; the added retained lifetime preserves this entry fence.) - `Scheduler shutdown timing` changes intended behavior with a stated reason (362cee12114d8a41b2b5eff42e96d973b6cfc327: One kernel scheduler synchronously fences timed work and joins running callbacks; the PR explains why cancellation must follow restart custody rather than coincide with fencing.) - `Restart persistence and settlement ordering` keeps the original intent (e051130c6ae044289990bb1045773c89f0014a87: Persist restart markers before database cleanup and retain finalizer ownership; the repair extends that ordering to retained ingress authority.) ### Testing Proof path: shipped entry point. ### Security None. ### Evidence What I checked: - **Current-main failure remains:** Fetched main still calls scheduler.beginClose before marker persistence and binds ingress authority to the request-entry shutdown signal, allowing shutdown to trigger queued-run revocation prematurely. ([`src/gateway/server-lifecycle.ts:533`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/aa4ebbb626c4dd6f5fad85e7bfc34d10e8c103fc/src/gateway/server-lifecycle.ts#L533), [aa4ebbb626c4](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/aa4ebbb626c4dd6f5fad85e7bfc34d10e8c103fc)) - **Ordering repair uses existing owners:** Request admission and scheduled wakeups close immediately; retained ingress authority and scheduler cancellation retire only after restart markers and session-stop classification. ([`src/gateway/server-lifecycle.ts:560`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/edb5215fe19524918581f59698d96af2f9738a51/src/gateway/server-lifecycle.ts#L560), [edb5215fe195](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/edb5215fe19524918581f59698d96af2f9738a51)) - **Compiled CLI and final-effect receipts:** Josh Avant supplies compiled CLI base-failure and candidate receipts covering distinct-process restart, exact queued writes in FIFO order, role downgrade, People removal, and app revocation before late tool effects; independent owner writes remain usable. ([4646580a4953](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/4646580a4953e6b600ca29624590ebe49f1446b5)) - **Proof remains applicable:** The subsequent commit adds admissionSignal to an integration-test fixture and changes its regression allocation from 271 to 272; production code is identical to the exercised candidate. ([`src/gateway/remote-control-ui-ingress.integration.test.ts:311`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/edb5215fe19524918581f59698d96af2f9738a51/src/gateway/remote-control-ui-ingress.integration.test.ts#L311), [edb5215fe195](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/edb5215fe19524918581f59698d96af2f9738a51)) - **Persistence and revocation regression:** The Gateway/SQLite regression verifies queued message bytes, original run and source identity, immediate admission refusal, and cancellation when the actual grant is revoked. ([`src/gateway/server-close.queued-inputs.test.ts:26`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/edb5215fe19524918581f59698d96af2f9738a51/src/gateway/server-close.queued-inputs.test.ts#L26), [edb5215fe195](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/edb5215fe19524918581f59698d96af2f9738a51)) - **Related merged repair has distinct scope:** https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/196540 preserves each queued input's source restrictions during replay; this PR repairs earlier shutdown cancellation that prevents those inputs from reaching replay. ([67a327fc1a32](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/67a327fc1a3294e34ffe8281a347ff74aacd5d2f)) ### PR surface Source +33, Tests +272, Docs +7, Other +3. Total +315 across 18 files. Added test files: 1.
View PR surface stats | Area | Files | Added | Removed | Net | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:| | Source | 8 | 48 | 15 | +33 | | Tests | 8 | 301 | 29 | +272 | | Docs | 1 | 7 | 0 | +7 | | Config | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | | Generated | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | | Other | 1 | 3 | 0 | +3 | | **Total** | **18** | **359** | **44** | **+315** |
### Preflight source Source unknown. Source comparison at the observed PR snapshot only. Completion is self-reported; body, policy, tests, execution, and report bytes are not verified. ### Review metrics | Metric | Value | Why it matters | |---|---|---| | **Production versus regression code** | Production +48/-15; tests/support +301/-29 | The production growth separates admission and retained authority within existing owners; regression growth covers persistence, real revocation, transport lifetime, and scheduler joins. | ### Labels Label changes: - add `rating: 🦞 diamond lobster`: Overall readiness is 🦞 diamond lobster; proof is 🦞 diamond lobster and patch quality is 🦞 diamond lobster. - remove `rating: 🐚 platinum hermit`: Current PR rating is `rating: 🦞 diamond lobster`, so this older rating label is no longer current. Label justifications: - `P2`: Accepted app messages can be silently lost during graceful restart, with impact limited to queued ingress work during shutdown. - `rating: 🦞 diamond lobster`: Overall readiness is 🦞 diamond lobster; proof is 🦞 diamond lobster and patch quality is 🦞 diamond lobster. - `status: 👀 ready for maintainer look`: ClawSweeper has no concrete contributor-facing blocker left for this PR. - `proof: sufficient`: Contributor real behavior proof is sufficient. ### Rating scale 6/6 🦀 challenger crab · 5/6 🦞 diamond lobster · 4/6 🐚 platinum hermit · 3/6 🦐 gold shrimp · 2/6 🦪 silver shellfish · 1/6 🧂 unranked krab. Overall follows the weaker of proof and patch quality; ✨ marks media proof (a screenshot, video, or linked artifact) that directly shows the changed behavior. ### Workflow ClawSweeper edits this one comment on every review. Comment `@clawsweeper re-review` for a fresh review only. Repair and merge execution lanes are retired. ### History
